source.title: Canada's National Artificial Intelligence Strategy: AI for All

wording: Neutral paraphrases of the supplied strategy for use as simulation stimuli. These are authored summaries, not verbatim government statements. Intended outcomes are attributed to the government; implementation and outcomes are not assumed.

privacy_protection.title: Consumer privacy reform
privacy_protection.text: The Government of Canada announces plans to modernize consumer privacy legislation. The proposed changes would recognize privacy as a fundamental right, strengthen people's control over their personal information, and protect children's information from exploitation. The government also plans to address inappropriate uses of personal data, including surveillance pricing.

online_safety.title: Online safety legislation
online_safety.text: The Government of Canada announces plans to introduce online safety laws addressing harms associated with digital technologies and AI. Its stated priorities include protecting children, providing legal tools to address deepfakes, making chatbot interactions safer, and holding those responsible for online harms accountable. It also commits to protecting elections against AI-enabled misinformation and foreign interference.

trusted_ai_certification.title: AI safety evaluation and certification
trusted_ai_certification.text: The Government of Canada announces plans to create a Canada Trusted AI Certification program intended to help people identify trustworthy AI products. It also commits CAD 50 million to expand the Canadian AI Safety Institute's work on emerging risks, technical research, and transparent evaluations of AI models.

ai_content_transparency.title: Identifying AI systems and generated content
ai_content_transparency.text: The Government of Canada announces that it will work on measures to make AI use more transparent, including capabilities such as watermarking AI-generated content. The stated aim is to help people recognize when they are interacting with an AI system or encountering AI-generated material.

ai_literacy.title: Free introductory AI education
ai_literacy.text: The Government of Canada announces plans for a National AI Literacy Initiative offering free introductory AI education accessible to all Canadians. Public libraries and community organizations would help deliver learning opportunities, including in rural, remote, and northern communities. The initiative would cover practical AI use as well as recognizing bias, misinformation, privacy risks, and unsafe uses.

student_ai_access.title: AI tools for postsecondary students
student_ai_access.text: The Government of Canada announces a commitment to give all postsecondary students access to trusted AI agents. It also plans to bring AI literacy content to one million students entering postsecondary education and provide classroom AI learning resources and training to more than 3,000 educators.

workforce_opportunities.title: AI-related employment and training
workforce_opportunities.text: The Government of Canada announces a plan to support up to 90,000 AI-related employment and work-placement opportunities by 2031 through student employment, skills, and Mitacs programs. It also plans to assess and expand employer-led AI training for workers in the middle of their careers, including people in skilled trades, working with employers, unions, colleges, and other training providers.

indigenous_led_ai.title: Indigenous leadership in AI
indigenous_led_ai.text: The Government of Canada announces plans to support Indigenous-led AI initiatives that strengthen Indigenous languages and cultural expression. It commits to working with Indigenous communities on their ability to shape how AI is developed and used in Indigenous contexts, including applications involving language, land management, and cultural heritage.

creative_technology.title: AI support for Canadian creators
creative_technology.text: The Government of Canada announces plans to establish a CAD 50 million Creative Technology Program. The program is intended to support Canadian creators in using AI on their own terms, as part of a wider commitment to represent Canadian voices, languages, and cultural knowledge in AI development and use.

official_languages.title: English and French in government AI
official_languages.text: The Government of Canada announces a commitment that AI systems deployed within government will perform equally well in English and French. It also plans to support the adoption of AI tools that protect and promote French, including its use in Quebec and Francophone minority communities elsewhere in Canada.

accessible_ai.title: Accessibility and inclusion in AI
accessible_ai.text: The Government of Canada announces plans to promote a national standard on accessible and equitable AI and to address accessibility barriers in AI systems. It also commits to applying Gender-Based Analysis Plus across AI policy, skills development, innovation, and governance, including attention to groups that experience disproportionate harms or barriers.

small_business_ai.title: Support for small-business AI adoption
small_business_ai.text: The Government of Canada announces plans to use the Business Development Bank of Canada's CAD 500 million LIFT program to help small and medium-sized businesses finance AI adoption. It also commits CAD 500 million to expand the Regional Artificial Intelligence Initiative, alongside tools and advice to help businesses identify uses for AI. The government sets a target for 60 percent of Canadian businesses to have adopted AI by 2034.

health_ai_mission.title: AI mission focused on healthcare
health_ai_mission.text: The Government of Canada announces plans for an AI Missions Program, with CAD 200 million committed to its first mission on improving health outcomes. The mission would bring together researchers, Canadian AI companies, governments, and healthcare practitioners. The government's stated goals include improving access to primary care, reducing emergency-room waits, preventing avoidable visits, and reducing administrative work for physicians.

health_data_infrastructure.title: Health-data platforms for research and AI
health_data_infrastructure.text: The Government of Canada announces plans to invest CAD 100 million in a Health Sector Data Space with the Canadian Institute for Health Information, linking secure, standardized health datasets for research and performance measurement. It also commits CAD 100 million to expand VITAL into five additional provinces, supporting the use of hospital clinical data for health research and AI development. The strategy commits to strong privacy protections for this data infrastructure.

government_ai_services.title: AI adoption in federal public services
government_ai_services.text: The Government of Canada announces plans to accelerate the procurement and deployment of AI in federal public services through the Office of Digital Transformation. Its stated aims include faster application processing and reduced administrative work. The government commits to transparency, privacy, and accountability standards, with human oversight of meaningful decisions and tasks, and plans a Prime Minister's Innovation Fellows Program to recruit technical expertise.

sovereign_ai_infrastructure.title: Canadian-controlled AI infrastructure
sovereign_ai_infrastructure.text: The Government of Canada announces plans to expand Canadian-controlled AI infrastructure, including a public supercomputer by 2031, domestic cloud services, and data centres. It will prioritize building key capabilities in Canada, while also partnering with trusted allies or purchasing existing solutions where appropriate. The strategy connects new data-centre development with clean-energy expansion, environmental standards, and benefits for local communities.

research_talent.title: AI research and talent recruitment
research_talent.text: The Government of Canada announces plans to expand the Canada CIFAR AI Chairs program from 130 to nearly 200 researchers and strengthen Canada's national AI institutes. It also plans to expand the Global Talent Stream to accelerate the arrival and onboarding of highly skilled AI workers and align permanent-residency measures with retaining recruited talent.

canadian_ai_company_growth.title: Financing and commercialization for Canadian AI companies
canadian_ai_company_growth.text: The Government of Canada announces plans for a CAD 500 million Canadian Tech Growth Fund to support the expansion of Canadian AI companies, including possible government equity investments. It also commits an additional CAD 700 million through the Compute Access Fund and CAD 130 million for commercialization programs at national AI institutes. Federal purchasing under the Buy Canadian policy would help provide customers for domestic firms.

international_ai_cooperation.title: International cooperation on sovereign AI
international_ai_cooperation.text: The Government of Canada announces plans to expand the Sovereign Technology Alliance launched with Germany. The alliance would coordinate work on AI models, digital infrastructure, research, safety evaluations, and procurement opportunities among participating countries. The government describes the alliance as a way to increase technological choice and reduce dependence on dominant technology ecosystems.

open_source_ai.title: Support for open-source AI
open_source_ai.text: The Government of Canada announces plans to work with other countries, researchers, civil society, industry, and AI institutes to sustain open-source AI development in the public interest. It also plans an inventory and shared library of AI tools to support adoption by researchers, small and medium-sized businesses, nonprofit organizations, and public-interest innovators.
